name: Marble Hornets
title: The Real Horror Behind Marble Hornets: How a YouTube Series Became Legend
claims: The first video was posted on June 20 2009, ten days after Eric Knudsen made the original Slender Man images. | 1
Marble Hornets was created by Troy Wagner, Joseph DeLage, and Tim Sutton. | 1
The series is a pseudo‑documentary based on the Slender Man mythos. | 1
There are 92 episodes on the Marble Hornets channel. | 1
As of late 2025, the channel had over 700 000 subscribers and 125 million views. | 1
The series established the Operator Symbol, also called the Proxy Symbol. | 1
Marble Hornets inspired other web series, giving rise to the “Slenderverse.” | 1
Wagner, DeLage, and Sutton have cited David Lynch works as inspiration. | 1
The initial budget was about $500. | 1
The first 26 episodes were planned on index cards. | 1
The series name came from a marble‑clad building and an exterminator van with “hornets” on it. | 1
It was filmed in Alabama using a single Handycam. | 1
The Operator’s first costume was made by duct‑taping flip‑flops together and covering the head with pantyhose (DeLage’s 2019 livestream). | 1
Tim Sutton created the coughing sound with a homemade synth. | 1
Entry #85’s fireball effect was achieved by pouring gasoline and water on a porch in one take. | 1
The crew had only one day to shoot entry #72 because the house was sold. | 1
The abandoned college in Season 3 was the only location they had permission to film. | 1
Marble Hornets amassed 97 episodes according to DVD commentary. | 1
In 2012, Blue Isle Studios partnered with the Marble Hornets team for the game Slender: The Arrival. | 1
A feature‑length film, Always Watching: A Marble Hornets Story, was released in 2015 and received predominantly negative reviews. | 1
Wagner has worked on Clear Lakes 44, ECKVA, and Marble Hornets: Rosswood. | 1
Crushable called Marble Hornets “by far the best of the bunch” in 2011. | 1
Dread Central named it one of its “Top 10 Horror Fan Films” in 2013. | 1
Early reports listed the channel at 250 000 subscribers and 55 million views for 65 episodes. | 2
Joblo reported a film adaptation was planned with Mosaic, Kirill Baru, John Zaozirny, and James Moran. | 2
The series synopsis from Joblo: a film student looks through canceled project tapes, discovers the Operator, and gets involved. | 2
